newsitem.title: BELGIUM: NATO studies four options for Bosnia.
newsitem.headline: NATO studies four options for Bosnia.

text.p: NATO ambassadors met on Monday to discuss four options for an international peace implementation force in Yugoslavia (IFOR) after its current mandate runs out on December 20.
Option A) No change. Under this plan IFOR's nearly 60,000 troops would remain in place as a deterrent and stabilising force.

Few if any favour this option because of the expense and the need to wean Bosnia off international intervention. The United States has said that it is willing to have only 8,500 of its troops in Bosnia next year, compared with 20,000 at IFOR's peak.
Option B) Reduced deterrent force with a mandate to prevent a new outbreak of fighting.
Favoured by many NATO military commanders, this option envisages between 25,000 and 30,000 troops in Bosnia maintaining a primarily military stance.

Option C) Reduced deterrent force with broader focus to help stabilise fledgling institutions. Fighting battalions would not be locally-based but rather operate as rapid-reaction force, flying in when needed.
This is the option NATO ambassadors are expected to endorse.
Option D) -- Total withdrawal. This option has been all-but ruled out, given the decision on Friday by the United States to remain in the region next year.
Carl Bildt, the international community's representative in Bosnia, has said that if IFOR was to withdraw now from Bosnia, war would break out "in the blink of an eye."
